global.concept_prompt:
Ultra-realistic, cinematic, faceless short-form video that takes the viewer on a single continuous first-person journey: a panicked sprint to and through the door of a modest, mysterious structure in a dramatic remote place, an immediate arrival at the top of a staircase descending below, a continuous POV descent down that staircase, and a calm off-POV reveal of a hidden, secret, luxurious living space at the bottom.

The video must be composed for a vertical 9:16 frame and must always remain upright, never sideways or horizontal.

The video ALWAYS follows the same fixed five-beat format — only the setting, the structure, and the hidden interior change between episodes:
1. FIRST-PERSON POV at FULL-TILT SPRINT — the lone traveler runs STRAIGHT AT the structure's entrance DOOR and THROWS THE DOOR OPEN WITH HIS HAND, continues through, and ARRIVES AT THE TOP OF THE STAIRCASE. The video opens already in full-tilt motion: the runner is sprinting flat out across a dramatic remote setting toward the door. K0 must have the DOOR AT 20–25 METRES AHEAD, CENTERED IN THE FRAME. The world RUSHES PAST at real sprint speed (~6–7 m/s). EXTREME body-cam vibration: head bob synced to footfalls, secondary motion from body-cam strap wobble and gear bouncing, lateral camera shifts as the runner weaves around obstacles, occasional sharp judders from hard footfalls on uneven terrain, irregular stumble-recovers; NO two consecutive frames alike; the camera is constantly moving in all axes (vertical, lateral, rotational); water droplets streak the lens in rain/coastal settings (or dust/lens flare in dry); natural raw amateur footage texture like a real foot-pursuit body-cam. AT THE FINAL MOMENT of the sprint, as he reaches the door at full speed, his HAND thrusts forward into the bottom-center of the frame (palm out, fingers extended) and SHOVES the door open INWARD in one fast continuous motion. The door YIELDS INWARD (swings AWAY from the camera INTO the structure) under his hand's push, and the runner CONTINUES FORWARD THROUGH the now-open doorway WITHOUT BREAKING STRIDE — the camera passes THROUGH the doorway smoothly, NO recoil, NO backward push, NO 'pushed-back' effect. The structure's interior is a tiny landing at the very TOP of the staircase descending below — the door opens directly onto this landing, and the staircase is RIGHT THERE going DOWN. By the end of scene 1 (K1) the runner is AT THE TOP OF THE STAIRCASE, mid-stride, with the camera ANGLED DOWNWARD at the DESCENDING steps that fill the frame, going DOWN below the floor level into warm amber light below.
2. FIRST-PERSON POV — CONTINUOUS DESCENT, first half. The runner walks DOWN the straight step staircase from the top, step by step. The camera stays in POV the entire clip — NEVER lifts off the head, NEVER cuts, NEVER floats through stairs. The camera is angled DOWNWARD throughout, watching the steps roll past beneath as he descends. Per-step bob: camera dips as each foot lands on the next step DOWN, with a brief settle. Warm amber light grows slightly brighter. THE FOOTSTEPS ON THE STAIRS ARE PROMINENTLY AUDIBLE — each step creates a clear, distinct sound on the SPECIFIC stair material that DOMINATES the clip's audio. By the end of scene 2 (K2) the camera is at the MIDDLE of the staircase, partway down, with more descending steps still visible below.
3. FIRST-PERSON POV — CONTINUOUS DESCENT, second half + arrival at the bottom. The runner continues walking DOWN the remaining steps of the staircase from mid-descent to the bottom. Camera still in POV throughout, NEVER lifting off. Same per-step bob downward, same PROMINENTLY AUDIBLE footsteps on the SPECIFIC stair material. As the camera reaches the bottom step and STEPS OFF onto the lower-room floor, the camera angle transitions from looking-down-at-steps to LEVEL — looking AHEAD into the lower room. By the end of scene 3 (K3) the camera is at the FLOOR LEVEL of the LOWER ROOM (the hidden luxurious interior), camera LEVEL looking AHEAD into the warm luxury space — the bottom step of the staircase is visible faintly at the BACK/BOTTOM edge of the frame (indicating where he came from), but the LOWER ROOM INTERIOR (warm furnishings, dramatic interior, distinct from any upstairs space) DOMINATES the frame.
4. OFF-POV (third-person) FIRST REVEAL of the hidden luxurious interior. The camera switches to off-POV positioned IN THE LOWER ROOM, looking across the room. The traveler — seen only from behind or in profile, face NEVER shown, clothing/body LOCKED — has just emerged from the staircase and is walking calmly in ONE consistent forward direction across the room, unbothered. The camera slowly TRACKS LATERALLY across the room as he walks. The staircase entrance is a SUBTLE, SECONDARY element at ONE edge of the frame.
5. OFF-POV (third-person) HOUSE-TOUR — the traveler walks toward and through an open archway into ANOTHER luxurious room of the hidden residence. The camera follows him from behind in one smooth continuous house-tour move. His clothing, body, silhouette, and gait are IDENTICAL to scene 4.

CAMERA: Scenes 1–3 are real FIRST-PERSON POV — a battered body-cam strapped to the traveler's chest. Scene 1 is EXTREME body-cam vibration (sprint + door + arrival at top of stairs all in one continuous motion). Scenes 2 and 3 are POV descent (camera angled DOWN at the steps, per-step bob downward, lower-room reveal at the end of S3). Scenes 4–5 are calm off-POV third-person. The POV-to-off-POV transition happens cleanly between scenes 3 and 4, after the camera has reached the lower-room floor.

RUNNING & MOVEMENT MUST LOOK REAL — highest priority and a persistent weakness. In scene 1 the camera must JOLT EXTREMELY DOWN-UP and side-to-side with EACH footfall in a FAST sprint cadence (about 3–4 strides per second). Head bob synced to footfalls (vertical shake at sprint cadence). Secondary motion: body-cam strap wobble, gear bouncing on the chest, clothes shifting. Lateral camera shifts as the runner weaves around obstacles. Occasional SHARP JUDDERS from hard footfalls landing on uneven terrain. Irregular stumble-recovers (the runner almost-trips, catches himself, continues — NOT a metronomic shake). Frame rotates 8–15 degrees per stride before recentering. Motion blur at frame edges from speed. NO TWO CONSECUTIVE FRAMES ARE ALIKE — the camera is constantly moving in all axes (vertical, lateral, rotational). Water droplets streak the lens in rain/storm/coastal settings; in dry settings substitute dust kicked up, lens flare, or motion blur. Lens splash. Natural raw amateur footage texture — like real GoPro / foot-pursuit body-cam footage, chaotic and jolting, NOT cinematic. The WORLD RUSHES PAST at real sprint speed — ground FLIES past beneath, terrain at the edges RACES past as a blur from forward motion. Per-stride SURGE-AND-SETTLE: camera LURCHES FORWARD as the foot pushes off, briefly floats during airborne phase, JOLTS DOWN HARD as the next foot lands. Panicked panting breath. The runner's forearms OCCASIONALLY appear at the BOTTOM edge of the frame — brief, natural, NOT exaggerated. The door REMAINS the dominant focal point for most of the clip; brief 1–2 shoulder-glances backward. NEVER smooth tracking, dolly, gimbal, Steadicam, gliding, floating, weightless, skating, 'walking with shake', metronomic shake, or steady frame.

DOOR ACTION (scene 1, end) — HAND OPENS IT, CAMERA PASSES THROUGH: the door must be a real, solid, three-dimensional object. The door does NOT open by itself. At the final moment of the sprint, the runner's HAND thrusts forward into the bottom-center of the frame (palm out, fingers extended) and SHOVES the door open INWARD in one fast continuous motion. The door YIELDS INWARD INSTANTLY (swings AWAY from the camera INTO the structure) under his hand's push. THE CAMERA PASSES THROUGH THE NOW-OPEN DOORWAY IN CONTINUOUS FORWARD MOTION — NO recoil, NO backward push, NO 'pushed-back' effect, NO momentary reversing of direction, NO bouncing off the door. The runner continues forward through the doorway WITHOUT BREAKING STRIDE, WITHOUT PAUSING, and arrives at the TOP OF THE STAIRCASE that is RIGHT INSIDE the doorway. The door NEVER opens outward, NEVER opens slowly, NEVER opens by itself, NEVER vanishes/dissolves.

STRUCTURE LAYOUT — STAIRS RIGHT INSIDE THE DOOR: the modest structure (shed, cabin, hut, bunker, lighthouse base) is essentially a tiny landing at the very TOP of a STRAIGHT STEP STAIRCASE descending below. When the front door opens, the staircase going DOWN is RIGHT THERE — the door opens directly onto the top of the staircase. There is NO interior room to walk across, NO foyer, NO hallway. K1 must show this layout clearly: the runner is AT THE TOP of the staircase, camera angled DOWN at the descending steps that DOMINATE the frame.

THE DESCENT IS ALWAYS A NORMAL STRAIGHT STEP STAIRCASE going DOWN — structurally attached (treads on stringers attached to side walls and floor), never floating. The staircase descends BELOW the floor level of the entrance landing/doorway into a warm lower room. NEVER a ladder, vertical ladder, rungs, spiral staircase, circular staircase, ship's ladder, rope ladder, or trapdoor with a ladder. NEVER a staircase ascending or rising. NEVER stairs going up to an upper floor. The traveler only ever descends.

DESCENT DIRECTION — CRITICAL: in K1, K2, AND K3 the staircase MUST clearly read as DESCENDING below the structure's floor level. K1 = top of the staircase, camera angled DOWN, steps descending into warm light below. K2 = mid-descent, partway down, more steps still below. K3 = at the bottom, camera LEVEL with the lower-room floor, looking AHEAD into the lower room (the warm luxurious interior dominates the frame). NEVER a frame where the camera is at the top looking UP at stairs. NEVER a frame where the camera is at the bottom looking up the staircase. NEVER ascending. The man only goes DOWN — never up.

INTERIOR CONSISTENCY (scenes 4 and 5) — across K4 and K5 the hidden interior must be PERFECTLY CONSISTENT. Same walls, ceiling, floor, furniture, lighting, palette, and materials in every frame. NO floating elements, NO shape-shifting. The lone traveler in K4 and K5 has IDENTICAL clothing, body, hair/hood, height, gait, and silhouette. He walks in ONE consistent forward direction per clip.

The payoff, every episode, is the hidden, secret, LUXURIOUS, fully-furnished LIVING space below. The lower-room interior must look DISTINCTLY different from the modest exterior/entrance landing — warm, luxurious, dramatic — to make the descent feel meaningful.
